title: Orbit and Static
premise: Zephyrine Underhill smuggles stolen memories through orbital customs while quietly maintaining a beacon whose original commissioning records have been erased. When gravity across the system stutters for nine seconds, he discovers the beacon was built to mask a countdown: the relay at the edge of dead space is broadcasting an inheritance claim left by his vanished mother, who once engineered the system's gravity lattice. Racing the signal's propagation, Zephyrine learns the ruling Consortium will kill to bury the truth that their power rests on stolen memory-tech his mother invented and they stole from her. At the relay, he must choose between destroying the lattice's control core — freeing the system but erasing every archived memory, including his own of her — or letting the Consortium keep its corrupted inheritance. He destroys it, keeping only one memory intact in his own head, and broadcasts the raw truth instead.
about_author: Paloma Almeida is a former radio astronomer who traded telescope shifts for fiction after a decade listening to signals nobody could explain. She writes from a coastal town in Portugal, where she still keeps a hand-painted chart of dead space above her desk.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A routine smuggling run past orbital customs goes wrong when gravity flickers for exactly nine seconds, scattering ships and exposing his hidden cargo of contraband memories. In the chaos, his beacon pings him with a signal it has never sent before. The emotional beat is disorientation curdling into dread: the universe itself just lied to him.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Paid For
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, with a flashback in his mother's voice embedded in an old memory chip. He investigates the beacon's maintenance logs and finds records scrubbed by someone with Consortium-level access — someone who knew his name before he was born. Emotional beat: the first crack in his carefully unattached life as loyalty to a ghost begins pulling at him.

chapters.title: Customs, and Other Predators
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Consortium inspector Vess Oka corners him over the gravity anomaly, offering leniency for information about the beacon. Zephyrine realizes the flicker wasn't an accident but a searchlight sweeping for something specific — him. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve as he chooses flight over cooperation.

chapters.title: Cargo of Other Lives
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV interwoven with fragments from the memories he carries, including a stranger's recollection of his mother alive and working for the Consortium. He decodes the beacon's true function: a dead-man switch tied to the gravity lattice's control core. Emotional beat: grief arriving late, twenty years overdue, for a mother he barely remembers.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. His patched-together ship makes the crossing toward dead space while Consortium hunters close in; a near-fatal reactor failure forces him to jettison most of his smuggled memories to survive. Emotional beat: the cost made physical — he has literally sold pieces of other people's pasts to buy his own future.

chapters.title: What Vess Oka Knows
chapters.summary: Vess Oka's POV. The inspector pursues Zephyrine but uncovers evidence that the Consortium ordered the beacon's records destroyed and his mother silenced. Torn between career loyalty and the truth surfacing under her, she makes a quiet choice: she lets his trail go cold and falsifies her report. Emotional beat: the antagonist's mirror — loyalty bending toward truth.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He reaches the derelict relay and finds his mother's final recording: proof the Consortium stole the lattice's memory-tech from her, then used it to rewrite public record and entrench their rule. The signal is minutes from propagating system-wide, which would trigger their scorched-earth failsafe. Emotional beat: awe and fury fused into purpose.

chapters.title: Inheritance, With Conditions
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Inside the control core, he faces his mother's terms: broadcast the truth and destroy the core, erasing every archived memory in the lattice — including hers, and his only copy of her face. Vess arrives, no longer hunting him but unable to stop the Consortium fleet inbound behind her. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized — what do we owe the dead versus the living?

chapters.title: The Weight of Everything Forgotten
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, climax. As Consortium marines breach the relay, he initiates the core's collapse, holding his mother's single memory in his own mind as the archive burns out around him. Gravity holds steady this time — because the lie holding it up is gone. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into inheritance finally claimed on his own terms.

chapters.title: Static, and a Clear Signal
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, coda weeks later. The raw truth circulates freely now, unownable, and the Consortium's monopoly cracks under ordinary people remembering what was taken. Zephyrine runs one last honest shipment — his mother's memory, copied and given away — then retires the beacon for good. Emotional beat: quiet peace; the smuggler finally delivers something worth more than contraband.
